newsitem.title: USA: NBA BASKETBALL - UTAH ROLLS PAST HOUSTON IN WEST CONFERENCE FINAL.
newsitem.headline: NBA BASKETBALL - UTAH ROLLS PAST HOUSTON IN WEST CONFERENCE FINAL.

text.p: The Utah Jazz celebrated Karl Malone's MVP Award on Monday by cruising past the Houston Rockets 101-86 in the opener of the NBA Western Conference finals to raise their 1997 home playoff record to a perfect 6-0.

Malone, who edged Michael Jordan to win his first NBA Most Valuable Player Award Sunday, was presented with the trophy before the start of the best-of-seven series to the sound of a thunderous ovation from adoring Utah fans.
"When this happened tonight it was unbelievable," Malone said of the award presentation.

"I was happy that it happened but I wanted to get it over with so I could settle down and play basketball," added Malone, who then went out and scored 21 points to lead the Jazz a step closer to their first-ever NBA Finals berth.

Jeff Hornacek scored 11 of his 19 points in the third quarter and John Stockton added 16 points and 13 assists for the Jazz, who also received 31 points from their bench, including 11 from rookie Shandon Anderson.
Utah was well rested but a bit rusty early, having finished off the Lakers in five games a full week earlier.
The Rockets, who ended a tough seven-game series with Seattle on Saturday, led 23-20 after the first quarter before fatigue and the Jazz caught up with them.
Utah took the lead for good early in the second quarter. They outscored Houston 29-17 in the quarter for a 49-40 edge at halftime and later led by as many as 21 points.

Houston centre Hakeem Olajuwon scored 30 points and pulled down 13 rebounds for the Rockets, but was held scoreless in the fourth quarter. Charles Barkley and Clyde Drexler combined for just 25 points -- 13 for Drexler and 12 for Barkley, who was guarded by Malone.
Malone left the game with a right hand injury late in the first half as he burned and blistered it sliding across the floor. "It was a pretty ugly burn," he said.
But Malone started strong in the second half.
He scored five points in a 10-3 burst that opened the third quarter. A jumper by Hornacek capped the run for a 59-43 lead with 7:10 left in the third.
A 7-0 surge by Houston helped cut the deficit to 63-54 before Hornacek scored eight straight points.

He made a layup, then buried a three-pointer after a backcourt steal by Howard Eisley. He then drew a foul from Mario Elie, who argued and got a technical foul. Hornacek made all three free throws, pushing the lead to 71-54.
The Rockets made one last surge, pulling within 81-72 with 10:52 to play. But Utah responded with eight in a row, including four by Malone, who also grabbed 13 rebounds.
"We want to forget this game," said Malone, "because Houston is Houston and they're going to come out and give us everything they've got in the second game."
Utah also hosts Game Two on Wednesday.
The Eastern Conference finals open Tuesday night as the defending NBA champion Chicago Bulls host the Miami Heat.
